This Appeal Coming On For Final Hearing, This

Coram: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice C M Joshi
 Oral Judgment

(PER: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE C M JOSHI) Heard the learned counsel for the appellants and the learned counsel for the respondent No.2.
02.
Being aggrieved by the judgment and award in MVC.No.1402/2016 dated 27.10.2021, by the Principal Senior Civil Judge and MACT-V, at Vijayapura, the petitioner is before this Court, in appeal.

03. The factual matrix of the case is that on 04.06.2015 at about 4:30 p.m. the son of the petitioners was traveling as a pillion rider on a motorcycle bearing NC: 2025:KHC-K:905 Reg.No.MH-12-AT-7040, near Bavada Chudachal, Nimaskhar Tq: Indapur Dist: Pune on Akluj-Pune road, Maharashtra
; the Mini Lorry bearing Reg.No.MH-42-T- 1036 came from opposite direction and collided with the motorcycle, resulting in the death of son of the petitioners by name Atul.
It is contended that the deceased was aged about 18 years and was earning Rs.10,000 per month.
The petitioners have lost their bread winner.

Therefore, they are entered for compensation from driver and owner of the offending vehicle i.e., Mini Lorry bearing Reg.No.MH-42-T- 1036.
04.

The petitioners also contended that the accident was due to negligence on the part of the driver of the mini lorry and therefore, the liability has to be fastened upon the owner and insurer of the vehicle.
05. Despite service of notice, respondent No.1 did not appear and as such, placed exparte.

Respondent No.2 Shivaji And Anr vs Rajendra And Anr on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24516544/
2 - Insurance Company appeared and filed written statement contending that the compensation claimed is NC: 2025:KHC-K:905 highly exorbitant, imaginary and untenable in law and denied the age, income and occupation of the deceased.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It also contended that the terms and conditions of the policy were violated by the driver of respondent No.1.

It was contended that the rider of the motorcycle was negligent and the owner and insurer of the motorcycle are also necessary parties to the petition and therefore, the petition is liable to be dismissed.
06. On the basis of the above pleadings, the Tribunal framed necessary issues for its consideration.
Petitioner No.1 was examined as PW.1 and a witness was examined as PW.2.
Exs. P1
to P10
were marked in their evidence.
An official of respondent No.2-Insurance Company was examined as RW.1 and Exs.R1 and R2 were marked on their behalf.

07. After hearing both sides, the Tribunal came to the conclusion that there was violation of the terms and conditions of the policy, since the driving licence of the driver of the mini lorry was not produced and therefore, it NC: 2025:KHC-K:905 held that the insurance company is not liable.
Hence, it has fastened the liability on respondent No.1-owner.
Holding so, it assessed the compensation payable to the petitioners at Rs.7,18,000/- by considering the notional income of the deceased at Rs.6,000/- per month.
08. Being aggrieved by the said judgment and award, the petitioners are before this Court in appeal.
09. Learned counsel appearing for the appellants has also filed an application-I.A.No.1/2024 under Order 41 Rule 27 of CPC, seeking to produce the additional evidence.
It is stated in the affidavit accompanying the application that, the driving licence of the driver of the offending vehicle was produced before the Tribunal, but due to oversight, it was not marked.

As such, the appellants are justified in filing the application under Order 41 Rule 27 of CPC to consider the said driving licence,
as it would render a great assistance to the Court in determining the liability to pay the compensation.
It is necessary to observe that though the application was filed NC: 2025:KHC-K:905 on 10.12.2024, no objections are filed to the same till date.

Since the document sought to be produced along with the application is also found in the Trial Court records and the Tribunal had not got it marked, the affidavit filed in support of the application has greater force.

Consequently,
I.A.1/2024 deserves to be allowed and the same is accordingly allowed.

10. A careful perusal of the records of the Tribunal would show that soon after the accident, a FIR was registered by the concerned police and ultimately, a charge sheet was also filed against the driver of the vehicle owned by respondent No.1.

It is pertinent to note that in the said charge sheet,
there is no such charge leveled against the driver of the vehicle for driving the same without a valid driving licence.
Therefore, the contention of the appellant that the driver of respondent No.1 had a valid driving licence as on the date of the accident gets support from the charge sheet also.
A perusal of the impugned judgment shows that the Tribunal had not bestowed its attention in respect of the documents, which were available in the file.

It simply accepted the version of RW.1 as Shivaji And Anr vs Rajendra And Anr on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24516544/
3 a gospel truth.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is also pertinent to note that the Tribunal has not bestowed its attention on the charge sheet also, where the offence of driving the vehicle without a valid driving licence was not alleged.

Therefore, when the document showing the fact that the driver of the offending vehicle had a valid driving licnece is available on record and said driving licence produced before the Tribunal was issued by none else than the police officer of Walchand Nagar Police Station, who had registered the FIR, fastening of the liability on respondent No.1 is prima facie unsustainable in law.

Therefore,
to that extent, there shall be interference by this Court.
Consequently, respondent No.2-Insurance Company is held liable to pay the entire compensation.

Learned counsel appearing for the appellants would submit that the Tribunal has not bestowed its attention to the requirement of law that there shall be future prospects that has to be added to the income of the deceased.

Though the Tribunal considers the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others1, it has not added the future prospects to the income of the deceased.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, considering the age of the deceased, 40% is to be added to the notional income of the deceased towards future prospects.
13. So far as the income of the deceased is concerned, the Tribunal has assessed the notional income at Rs.6,000/- p.m.

The guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority in respect of the settlement of the claims arising out of the motor vehicle accidents before the Lok Adalath prescribes the notional income at Rs.8,000/- p.m. for the year 2015.

In umpteen number of (2017)
16 SCC 680 NC: 2025:KHC-K:905 cases, this Court has held that the said guidelines issued by the KSLSA are in general conformity with the wages fixed under the Minimum Wages Act.

Therefore,
the notional income of the deceased is held to be Rs.8,000/- p.m.

Hence, the loss of dependency is calculated as:
Rs.8,000 + Rs.3,200 (i.e., 40% future prospects) x 12 x 18 x 50% = Rs.12,09,600/-.
14.

So far as the compensation under the conventional heads i.e., loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses is concerned, it is relevant to note that the Apex Court in the case of Pranay Sethi supra has held that there shall be escalation of 10% for every three years.
Such judgment was rendered in the year 2017.
Obviously, on account of variation in the price index and inflation of the money value, the enhancement of 10% for every three years was suggested.
Accordingly, in the year 2020, there shall be one enhancement, but the compensation being determined in the year 2025

,
obviously, there shall be 3 such escalations.

In the light of - 10 - NC: 2025:KHC-K:905 the same, a sum of Rs.70,000/-, which has been awarded by the Tribunal under the heads of loss of consortium, funeral expenses and loss of estate shall have to be enhanced by 30% i.e., Rs.21,000/-.

Hence, the compensation is reassessed as below:
Loss of dependency Rs.12,09,600/-
Loss of Consortium Rs. 40,000/-

sentences.text:
Loss of estate Rs. 15,000/-
Funeral expenses Rs. 15,000/-
Escalation 30% Rs. 21,000/-

Less: awarded by Tribunal Rs. 7,18,000/-
Enhancement Rs. 5,82,600/-
Thus, the appellants are entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.5,82,600/- with interest and therefore, the appeal deserves to be allowed in part.

Hence, the following:
ORDER (i) The appeal is allowed in part.

(ii) The impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is modified by awarding a sum of Rs.5,82,600/-in addition to what - 11 - NC: 2025:KHC-K:905 has been awarded by the Tribunal together with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization excluding the interest for a delayed period of 248 days in filing the appeal.
(iii) Respondent No.2-Insurance Company is directed to deposit the entire compensation amount within a period of six weeks from the date of this order.
(iv) Rest of the order passed by the Tribunal remains unaltered.
Sd/-
